claims.explanation: Piperacetazine is a phenothiazine dopamine-receptor antagonist that also binds PAX3::FOXO1 and inhibits squalene epoxidase (SQLE), disrupting cholesterol/lipid metabolism; the selective killing pattern is best explained by dependency on SQLE-driven sterol synthesis and on RTK/RAS-PI3K-MAPK signaling that is co-targeted by its dopamine-receptor/GPCR antagonism. Lines with activating EGFR, BRAF, NRAS, KRAS, PTEN loss, or NF1 loss are sensitized, while lines with intact FBXW7 or alternative survival wiring are relatively protected.

features.basis: Piperacetazine is a competitive SQLE inhibitor; high SQLE expression predicts dependence on the cholesterol-synthesis pathway it blocks (PMID 41093921)
Activating EGFR mutations appear in multiple selectively killed lung lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) and EGFR signaling is a shared dependency
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines (K029AX, UACC62, SNUC5) are among the most killed, consistent with MAPK-pathway addiction
NRAS-mutant KU1919 is selectively killed, suggesting RAS-MAPK dependence sensitizes to the drug
KRAS-mutant pancreatic lines (SNU410, T3M4) are among the most killed
PTEN loss (FTC133, KALS1, UACC62, 786O, ZR751) is enriched in the most-killed lines, consistent with PI3K-AKT dependence
NF1 loss (FTC133, BICR6, KALS1) hyperactivates RAS-MAPK and appears in killed lines
Piperacetazine directly binds and inhibits PAX3::FOXO1 transcriptional activity in alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (PMID 37732905)
PAX3::FOXO1 fusion is the direct binding target of piperacetazine (PMID 37732905)
FBXW7-mutant lines (CL11, NCIH1648, SNUC5 exception) are enriched among least-affected lines, suggesting intact FBXW7-mediated turnover is not required for survival under drug pressure
Annotated dopamine receptor antagonist activity; DRD2-expressing lines may be more responsive to the drug's GPCR-mediated effects
TP53 mutation is nearly universal across both killed and protected lines, so it is not selective; listed only to note lack of discriminating value
